name: Lian Weizhou
current_role: Former CEO and co-founder, Longtop Financial Technologies (Xiamen; NYSE-delisted 2011); current role unknown
profile: Co-founded Longtop with Jia Xiaogong in Xiamen in 1996, building it into a software and IT-services provider for Chinese banks that listed on the NYSE in 2007. The company was delisted in 2011 and he has kept no public profile since.
interesting_fact: Longtop was one of the largest Chinese software firms serving the banking sector when it listed on the NYSE in 2007.
notes: Longtop collapsed in 2011 amid an accounting-fraud scandal and SEC litigation; no public presence or contact found since. Not a recommended outreach target.

name: Ajay S Shriram
current_role: Chairman & Senior Managing Director, DCM Shriram Ltd (New Delhi)
profile: Indian industrialist who leads DCM Shriram, the diversified group spanning chloro-vinyl chemicals, sugar, fertilisers, Shriram Farm Solutions and Bioseed. A B.Com graduate of Sydenham College, Bombay, he also attended Harvard Business School's Program for Management Development, and he was president of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in 2014-15.
interesting_fact: He chairs the Governing Body of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC), the Delhi college his family founded, and chairs the board of IIM Sirmaur.
deep_cut_fact: Before leading CII, he was President and Chairman of the Paris-based International Fertilizer Industry Association (2009-11), and earlier he chaired the Fertilizer Association of India (2000-02).
notes: The press email is DCM Shriram's published Corporate Communication/CSR contact (Ms. Aman Pannu). The group's chlor-alkali business is power-intensive and runs captive power plants, which could make a good energy angle.

name: Hanwant Manbir Singh
current_role: Former director, Karamtara Engineering (Mumbai), appointed 2001 and ceased 22 June 2023 per MCA-derived records; still lists directorships in Karamtara Steel and Karamtara Fasteners
profile: Member of the Singh family behind Karamtara Engineering, a Mumbai-area maker of transmission-line towers, solar mounting and tracker structures, and fasteners. The company is run by promoters Tanveer Singh (CMD) and Rajiv Singh, and it received SEBI approval in 2025 for a Rs 1,750 crore IPO.
interesting_fact: Karamtara says in its DRHP that it is India's largest producer of solar mounting structures and tracker components, and it also builds lattice towers for power transmission lines.
notes: Very low public profile, and his exact relation to the current promoters isn't documented in sources I could verify. The role comes from MCA-aggregator data (tofler/qorpiq). Karamtara's grid and solar-structures business fits the energy theme, but the promoters Tanveer or Rajiv Singh are the more visible route.

name: Hu Jirong
current_role: President (总裁), Xingyue Group Co., Ltd. (星月集团), Yongkang, Zhejiang
profile: Co-founded Xingyue with his brother Hu Jishen in 1989 as a small aluminium-ingot workshop in Gushan, Yongkang. It grew into a group of more than 10 companies making motorcycle engines, security doors, tools, carpets and appliances. Under his leadership it has moved into agricultural machinery, pharmaceuticals and silk-based regenerative-medicine devices, and the group reports assets above RMB 8bn.
interesting_fact: In 1996 Xingyue produced China's first GY6-125 scooter engine, and its engines went on to power more than 500 Chinese motorcycle makers. The same year it formed a joint venture with an ordnance-industry plant in Luoyang, which the company calls the first such tie-up between a military enterprise and a private firm in China.
deep_cut_fact: Xingyue started on 6 August 1989 with RMB 750,000 and 12 workers in a 100 m2 workshop. Its first breakthrough came in 1993 with the 147FM motorcycle cylinder head, which won gold at the 1995 China high-tech new products expo. Hu Jirong was also a deputy to the 10th National People's Congress and is honorary principal of Gushan Primary School.
notes: Chinese-language outreach advised. The group publishes office phone lines but no group-level press email (subsidiary sales emails only). His 'President's message' is at http://www.xingyue.com/president.html.

name: Keith A Hutton
current_role: Director and co-founder, TXO Partners, L.P. (Fort Worth, TX; NYSE: TXO)
profile: Petroleum engineer who spent about 25 years at XTO Energy and became its CEO in December 2008, running it through the $41bn ExxonMobil acquisition in 2010. In 2012 he co-founded TXO Partners (formerly MorningStar Partners) with Bob Simpson and served as its CEO until 2022, then as President of Production & Development until November 2024. He remains a director and holds about 9% of the units.
interesting_fact: He led XTO Energy, one of the biggest US natural-gas producers, at the point ExxonMobil bought it for $41bn in 2010, a defining deal of the shale-gas era.
deep_cut_fact: Before XTO he spent five years with Sun Oil Company in both its international and domestic divisions (1982-87). Texas A&M named him a Harold Vance Department of Petroleum Engineering Distinguished Graduate in 2009.
notes: Low personal media profile. Best route is TXO investor relations, or via the co-founder and chairman Bob Simpson.

name: Karuturi Satyanarayana Murthy
current_role: Executive Chairman and co-promoter, Apex Frozen Foods Ltd (Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh; NSE/BSE: APEX)
profile: Andhra Pradesh aquaculture entrepreneur (born 1955) with more than 30 years in the shrimp business. He co-promoted Apex Frozen Foods, a vertically integrated exporter of farmed Pacific white shrimp to the US, EU and UK that listed in 2017. Long its chairman and MD, he was reappointed Executive Chairman from 1 December 2025, with K. Subrahmanya Chowdary as MD.
interesting_fact: Apex runs a Kakinada processing plant of about 9,240 MTPA and its own shrimp hatchery and farming operations, and supplies frozen and ready-to-cook shrimp to major Western retailers and distributors.
deep_cut_fact: Apex began in 1995 as a partnership firm exporting shrimp from a leased processing facility, and only built its own plant at Kakinada in 2004, almost a decade later.
notes: Low media profile. The company's IR agency, Stellar IR, is also listed on the contact page. This is a food business, so the fit with the energy/data-center theme is weak.

name: S Senthilnathan
current_role: Director, Rasi Seeds Pvt Ltd (Attur/Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu); previously Director-Finance
profile: Sengottuvelu Senthilnathan is a director of Rasi Seeds and son-in-law of its founder, Dr M. Ramasami. Rasi was founded in Attur in 1973 and became India's leading cotton-hybrid seed company, and it was the largest seller of Bt cotton seed in India in the mid-2000s. He joined the board in 2003 and handled finance.
interesting_fact: Rasi was the first Indian seed company to pay an upfront fee for Bt technology, in 1999. Its RCH 2 Bt hybrid was approved in 2004, and by 2006 it had overtaken Mahyco as India's largest Bt cotton seed seller.
notes: Very private, with almost no personal media footprint. The only published email is Rasi Seeds' general customer-care address. The founder, Dr M. Ramasami, is the public face of the business.

name: Bradley Bauer
current_role: Partner, Co-CEO and Co-CIO, Värde Partners (global alternative credit investor; Minneapolis/New York)
profile: Brad Bauer joined Värde in 2007, became a partner in 2013 and was named Co-CEO alongside Ilfryn Carstairs in October 2023. He also oversees private-markets investing as Co-CIO. He appears as a 10% owner of Nabors Industries (NBR) only because he is a reporting person on Värde funds' filings after Nabors bought Parker Wellbore in 2025, and he disclaims beneficial ownership beyond his pecuniary interest.
interesting_fact: Värde, founded in Minneapolis in 1993, has invested more than $100bn across credit markets. Bauer co-leads it under a deliberate US/Asia co-CEO structure with Singapore-based Carstairs, with whom he had worked for more than 16 years by 2023.
notes: The SEC 'TenPercentOwner' flag on Nabors reflects Värde fund holdings, not a personal stake. Route through Värde Communications & Public Affairs. He is a frequent speaker at private-credit conferences such as SuperReturn and the Milken Institute.
